html:
SMTO-EXE-0155 — The desktop step was stopped before it finished

GUID: b8da29a2-ba51-5c68-a3b2-28855760afb3
Slug: ui-operation-cancelled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • The desktop step was cancelled, usually because the task was stopped or the Gateway was shutting down. No click or typing from this step was sent to the app.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you selected Stop on this task yourself, you don't need to do anything else. This message only confirms the desktop step ended before it sent any input.
  2. If you didn't stop it, look at the app on the Gateway's computer and tell SMTO in the conversation what should happen next. SMTO never repeats a stopped step on its own, so it needs your go-ahead.
  3. If an earlier step in this task said its result was unknown, check the app for that change before asking SMTO to continue. Earlier steps may have changed the app even though this one did not.

What success looks like

  • The task either stays stopped as you intended or continues from what the app currently shows.

If it still fails

  • If desktop steps keep getting cancelled when nobody stopped them, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway; the Gateway may be restarting or shutting down.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Desktop UI service observed cancellation (a run stop or Gateway service shutdown) at a checkpoint before native input began, so the operation ended as cancelled with executed=false.

What this means

  • UI cancellation was observed at a checkpoint or outer wait; the mutation-start boundary determines whether the result is cancelled or outcome unknown. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • UI cancellation was observed at a checkpoint or outer wait; the mutation-start boundary determines whether the result is cancelled or outcome unknown.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original cancellation receipt, mutation-start evidence and current input gate state.

How to fix it

  • No native input was dispatched for this execution_id. Use the Gateway log to confirm whether cancellation came from a run stop or a service shutdown, check other receipts in the run for effect_unknown, and reconcile those with ui.snapshot or ui.element before issuing new input under a new execution_id.
  • The operation was cancelled. Check its effect_unknown flag before issuing another action.

Retry and execution caution

  • The operation was cancelled. Check its effect_unknown flag before issuing another action.

How to verify the fix

  • The original call settles without overlapping new input, and any effect is reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
